title: A remark on the majorizing measures theorem for general processes
summary: We show that the lower bound in the majorizing measures theorem holds for a large class of random vectors. Specifically, suppose $X \sim μ$ is a centered random vector in $\mathbf{R}^n$ with \[ C_{\mathrm{KL}}(μ) = \sup_{\substack{θ\neq η\\ θ, η\in \mathbf{R}^n}} \frac{\mathrm{KL}(μ_θ\| μ_η)}{\|θ- η\|_2^2} < \infty, \] where $μ_θ$ denotes the law of the translate $θ+ X$.
